title: MYTHS about Heat Pumps!
summary: HVAC contractor explains how electric backup and dual-fuel systems bring on backup heat, and says modern heat pumps no longer struggle below 40°F.

assertions.quote: the heat pump draws less electricity than when those heat strips turn on

verdicts.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see positive bill savings in 95-100% of cases with median savings of $300-$650 a year at any efficiency level.
Switching homes with electric resistance heaters to heat pumps almost always produces a clear benefit, even after capital cost, especially in large older homes in cold climates.

In Edwards' county model, heating with electricity (taken as resistance) or non-gas fuels is generally more expensive, so the bill savings from a heat pump are largest there; heat pumps are cited as 3-5 times more efficient than resistance.
Against electric resistance baselines, the ductless and all-electric ducted heat pumps cut electricity use 46-56% with average cost savings of 53%, measured by alternating modes in the same homes.

Mini-splits stayed above COP 1.0 on average at nearly all outdoor temperatures, so they 'will nearly always be less expensive to operate than electric resistance heat'; the margin narrows to about 1.5x at the coldest temperatures.

In the UK sample, the change in electricity use after a heat pump was lowest, indeed negative, for households that previously used electric heating, so the heat pump used less electricity than the resistance heat it replaced (a small subgroup).
Heat pumps use up to 65% less energy than standard electric baseboard heating (NRCan), so switching from baseboards brings significant savings on the power bill.

assertions.quote: unlike a dual fuel system it's not going to turn off the outdoor unit the outdoor unit's still going to run

verdicts.note: Standard heat pump controls stage resistance strips on top of the running compressor, unlike dual-fuel lockout.
All-electric systems let the heat pump run wherever possible with resistance boosting it, unlike fixed-changeover propane systems, so the heat pump met more of the load: annual COP 1.9 versus 1.3.

Below the switchover temperature the cold-climate units mostly ran heat pump plus staged auxiliary heat (supplemental mode), with auxiliary-only operation minimal above 0 F, and staging used the smallest element needed.

assertions.quote: a lot of thermostats have backup timers

verdicts.note: Lockout controls prevent strip heat above a set outdoor temperature, a requirement in the IECC.
Auxiliary energy largely tracked each site's auxiliary lockout temperature, with little use in the bin just above it; the exceptions were a faulty unit and an undersized one.

The thermostat's switchover setpoint sets the outdoor temperature above which auxiliary heat may not be called; observed switchover temperatures were higher than optimal because of programming and setbacks.

assertions.quote: if it got below 40 degrees outside heat pumps started to struggle to provide heat but those days are over
